an1.1:1.1: This translation is meant to deliberately echo the English idiom “So I hear, so I’ve heard”. It means that it has been passed down in oral tradition.
an1.1:2.1: Technically, it is not the sight that “occupies” the mind (literally “having invaded, remains”), but the unskillful qualities provoked by the sight ([an8.63:1.7]()). Hence this does not occur for one free of desire ([an6.55:17.1]()). As to what might have prompted such a strong statement, at [an5.55]() a similar passage is spoken in response to a mother and son, who, while ordained as monk and nun, had sex with each other.
